query: Starting from a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies, what single intervention could overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness while retaining or increasing strength? The hypothesis should address the tendency for dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries to produce local stress concentrations, microcracking, and catastrophic damage during straining. Specify the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted strength and ductility relative to the untreated starting material, the applicable testing and operating conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled amount of lattice distortion through ion irradiation can enhance the room-temperature tensile ductility of a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies, while retaining or increasing its strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies
generation.intervention: Ion irradiation to introduce controlled lattice distortion
generation.mechanism: Reduced dislocation pile-up and stress concentrations near internal boundaries
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved ductility and retained or increased strength
generation.boundary: Applicable to eutectic high-entropy alloys with similar microstructures
generation.uncertainty: Effects of ion irradiation on other material properties, such as corrosion resistance or high-temperature strength
generation.falsification_experiment: Tensile testing of ion-irradiated samples, with and without controlled lattice distortion, to compare ductility and strength

Question: How to achieve a simultaneous balance of high fracture strength and high ductility in high-entropy alloys while overcoming inferior castability and compositional segregation?. System: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 (atomic portion) eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA). Processing: Vacuum induction melting of commercially pure elements (Al, Co, Ni: 99.9 wt.%; Cr, Fe: 99.5 ~ 99.6 wt.%) in a BN crucible; heating to 600°C for 1 hour; pouring at 1500°C into a MgO crucible (220 mm length, 62 mm upper ID, 50 mm bottom ID) under argon atmosphere (0.06 MPa); bulk ingot weight ~2.5 kg.. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile tests at strain rate 1 × 10−3 s−1; elevated temperature tests at 600°C and 700°C at strain rate 1 × 10−3 s−1; cold rolling with 8% thickness reduction followed by tensile testing at 2 × 10−3 s−1..
